recorded_before: any fold of this row; the harness digests this file into every result.json
why_zero: every arm runs the identical 200-step, 3-recycle, 1-sample, seed-0 configuration on the same committed fixture and the same 35-row A3M. Nothing is optimised, no device cycle is deleted, and the only thing that varies is the clock.

anchor.source: c10-bare-baseline, bc66f7d6d, 16 accepted folds per size, during-sampled min = max = 1350 MHz
anchor.historical_fit: T = 2.901 + 15355/f, which reads 14.275 s at 1350 and 21.95 s at 800 -- it under-predicts the measured 1350 point by 0.61 s, so it is used only to bracket the prediction
anchor.clock_sweep_refit: perf/c10_orchestrator/fit_reexam, a0879f8f1, F = 3.478 s, a 512/298 work ratio of 1.839

predicted_F_size_dependence: F should be SMALLER at 298 aa than at 512 aa if it is dominated by featurization and CIF writing, which scale with the target. A strictly size-independent F would say the fixed term is host or dispatch overhead that does not see the target at all.
predicted_structure: byte-identical CIF in every arm at both sizes, so every pairwise float64 Kabsch RMSD is at float64 noise, far under the 0.60 A bar at 512 aa (user seed floor 1.84 A) and the 0.35 A bar at 298 aa (archived upstream seed pairs 0.741-0.847 A). A clock change that moves the structure is a finding and a STOP.
refutation: fitted F at or below 0 s
fitted F at or above 9.680 s, the whole 298 aa fold at 1350 MHz
a cell-median residual at 1200 or 1000 MHz above max(A/A timing floor, 0.05 s)
a during-fold clock that is not exactly that arm's own requested target

demand_arithmetic_stated_in_advance.F_untouched: reaching 10.0 s at 1350 MHz allows 1350*(10.0-F) Mcycles, so the cut is C - 1350*(10.0-F)
demand_arithmetic_stated_in_advance.F_cut_to_1s: reaching 10.0 s at 1350 MHz with F = 1.0 s allows 12150 Mcycles, so the cut is C - 12150
demand_arithmetic_stated_in_advance.if_F_exceeds_10s: no cycle cut whatsoever reaches the target and the campaign is a host problem, not a kernel problem
